title: Weather and seasons
description: Talk about heat, rain, cold and storms, say how the weather feels to you, and name the seasons.

guide.title: Weather happens
guide.text:
There is no 'it' in Bengali weather sentences. The weather itself is the subject, and it happens, falls, rises or gives.

বৃষ্টি (brishti) rain: বৃষ্টি হচ্ছে or বৃষ্টি পড়ছে, 'rain is happening / falling'.
রোদ (rod) sunshine: রোদ উঠেছে, 'the sun has come out'.
মেঘ (megh) cloud: মেঘ করেছে, 'it has clouded over'.
হাওয়া (haaowaa) wind: হাওয়া দিচ্ছে, 'the wind is blowing' (in Bangladesh the usual word is বাতাস, baataash).
ঝড় (jhor) storm: ঝড় আসছে, 'a storm is coming'.
কুয়াশা (kuyaashaa) fog: কুয়াশা পড়েছে।

Heat and cold 'fall' too: গরম পড়েছে, 'the hot weather has set in'; ঠান্ডা পড়েছে, 'it has turned cold'.

A plain description needs no verb: আজ খুব গরম, 'it is very hot today'; আকাশ পরিষ্কার, 'the sky is clear'.

guide.title: How it feels to you
guide.text:
To say that YOU feel hot or cold, use লাগা 'to strike, to feel' with yourself in the possessive: আমার গরম লাগছে, 'I feel hot'; আমার ঠান্ডা লাগছে, 'I feel cold'.

Do not say আমি গরম or আমি ঠান্ডা: that describes your temperature to the touch, or your temper.

The same verb gives liking: শীতকাল আমার ভালো লাগে, 'I like winter'.

And with the perfect, catching a cold: আমার ঠান্ডা লেগেছে।

guide.title: Six seasons
guide.text:
The Bengali year traditionally has six seasons of two months each:

গ্রীষ্ম (greeshsho) summer - the hot months before the rains
বর্ষা (borshaa) the monsoon
শরৎ (shorot) early autumn - clear skies, the season of Durga Puja
হেমন্ত (hemonto) late autumn - harvest
শীত (sheet) winter
বসন্ত (boshonto) spring

In everyday talk three matter most, with কাল (kaal) 'season, time' attached: গরমকাল (goromkaal) the hot season, বর্ষাকাল (borshaakaal) the rainy season, শীতকাল (sheetkaal) the cold season.

The Bengali new year, পয়লা বৈশাখ (poylaa boishaakh), falls in mid-April at the start of summer.
